newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds pullback, N.Z. outshines.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds pullback, N.Z. outshines.

text.p: Australian bonds outperformed the long-end of the U.S. market as its continued to pull back some of the sharp spread widening seen midweek, but remained outpaced by New Zealand debt.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread had started the week below 100 basis points, a level not seen in over 2-1/2 years, but this margin quickly expanded after the Reserve Bank dampened down intense speculation of an early policy easing.

"We've lost a bit of ground on the spread. Next week is going to be critical as to whether we outperform or underperform by international comparison and what the Reserve Bank does in early November, if anything," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.

Next week sees September quarter headline and underlying inflation on Wednesday and the August quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) on Thursday, which are seen as major factors as to whether the central bank eases policy from current 7.0 percent official interest rates.

Meanwhile, the New Zealand market continued to go from strength to strength. Having stood at a 50 basis point premium over Australia at the start of the week on the 10-year margin, it now stands at its lowest discount since late July.
A stock shortage at the short end of the N.Z. market helped to maintain this week's post election and weak CPI data rally.
